research_question: What does the leading string in each R5-observed legacy node_fills [string, object] record represent?

point_in_time_target.historical_source_requirement: Prefer immutable official evidence published before the legacy object date when available.

primary_source_evidence.claim: --write-fills streams fills in the API fills format to node_fills/hourly/{date}/{hour}.
--batch-by-block changes the write-* output from one event per line to one block per line; therefore the unbatched writer is documented as one event per line.

claims: Fill is a fill object whose defined fields include coin, px, sz, side, time, startPosition, dir, closedPnl, hash, oid, crossed, fee, tid and feeToken.
The Fill type does not contain a user field.
UserFillsData contains user separately from fills: {user, isSnapshot, fills}.
user_fills accepts an onchain address in 42-character hexadecimal format.
The userFills request passes that address in the separate user field.
The returned fill objects are documented without an embedded user field.
userFills subscriptions are keyed by subscription.user.
userFills messages are routed by ws_msg.data.user.

primary_source_evidence.title: Historical data
claims: older node_fills data is in a different format.

directly_documented_facts: Before the target object date, Hyperliquid documented --write-fills as writing API-format fills.
Before the target object date, Hyperliquid documented unbatched write output as one event per line.
Before the target object date, the official SDK represented user separately from Fill in userFills websocket data.
Before the target object date, the official SDK documented user_fills input as a 42-character onchain address and returned fill objects without an embedded user field.
R5 empirically observed every legacy node_fills record as [string, object] with a fill-like object shape.
reasoning.inference: The convergent primary-source explanation is that the leading string is the Hyperliquid user/onchain account address associated with the fill object.
reasoning.why_not_direct_proof: The public node repository documents writer behavior but does not expose the node serializer implementation that would directly name the first tuple element, and R5 intentionally retained no leading-string values or lexical-shape aggregates.

claims_proven: The historical official write-fills documentation, batching documentation and SDK interface model predate the 2025-07-27 target object.
The R5 object-side structure is strongly correspondent with the historical official SDK Fill shape.
The official API/SDK model keeps the user identity outside the Fill object and represents it as an onchain address.
claims_not_proven: The exact unpublished node serializer variable name or tuple type for the leading string.
That every R5 leading string lexically matches the 42-character 0x-prefixed address pattern.
Any specific wallet address contained in the archive object.
Alpha, market-data suitability or live-trading suitability.

next_minimum_empirical_gate_if_required.purpose: Resolve the remaining lexical-shape gap without retaining any wallet address or payload value.
next_minimum_empirical_gate_if_required.target: the same exact R5-bound legacy object only
